name: XDK Direct3D 8 (D3D8, D3D8LTCG)
_why: RECOMP_PB_EXEC: the pushbuffer executor draws what D3D wrote. RECOMP_VBLANK=paced: D3D's vblank handler keeps
the count the XMV player's clock and the swap counters read (without it: one flip, movies stuck on frame 1).
d3d8.c services D3D's GPU semaphore and software methods once the title gives their addresses (params):
see the comment at its top. Seen on: Fable 4D5300D1, Burnout 3 4541005B (XDK 5849), KOTOR 4C410003 (XDK 5455,
device found at run time through its slot at device - 8, fence event +0x19AC).
No XBA_D3D_DMA_WALK for D3D8 5455 (decided 2026-11-12, K-7): KOTOR's menu and character generation under 8 host
busy loops, 5 runs with the segment scan and 5 with RECOMP_PB_WALK=dma, title-built KEVENTs on: 0 freezes either
way; software method 5 came under the segment scan too (serviced in 3 of 5 scan runs, 2 of 5 walk runs), and no wait
for it was left hanging; fps medians overlapped (scan 14-38, walk 16-47). The latch spin that made
D3D8LTCG 5849 need the walk (profiles/xdk/d3d8ltcg) was not seen. RECOMP_PB_WALK=dma stays the fallback to try.
XBA-106: RECOMP_VBLANK=paced is also a runtime default (recomp_xdk_defaults.c), RECOMP_PB_EXEC already was
(templates/new-game main(), the Android shell). applies.imports: D3D's video mode and GPU calls (AvSetDisplayMode,
AvSendTVEncoderOption, Av{Get,Set}SavedDataAddress, MmClaimGpuInstanceMemory) pick this layer, and with it
d3d8.c (device found at run time, software methods), when the library table names no D3D8: a first guess, to
check on the library triage (XBA-63). d3d8.c finds no device in a title without D3D and stays idle there.
